item.title: Bastidas Soccer Academy Training Camp — Tue Aug 4, 9:00 AM — Manheim Central Middle School
item.description:
Established in 1999, the Bastidas Soccer Academy emphasizes the importance of basic skill and ball mastery. We are passionate about teaching you to have fun and develop a winning attitude. All boys and girls from any school or district, entering grades 3-8, are invited to attend this premier camp to kick off the fall season. Registration is $200 per player (or $190 each for a sibling group) and will include:
Camp T-shirt USSF Licensed Coaches (including “A” License coach Trajano Bastidas) and USYS ODP Coaches Camp features– league play, king of the hill, soccer dance, small sided games, stations Main focuses– first touch, passing, receiving, finishing, having fun!
Players should arrive at least 10 minutes early each day with proper attire, sneakers, cleats, shin guards, plenty of water, and a snack for the mid-point break. Questions? item.title: Evansburg Park — Sun Aug 9, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Walking Tails This walk goes out to the northeast about 1.25 miles and then we come back the way we came, for a total of 2.5 miles. The trail is a paved surface and fairly shady.
We will be meeting at the parking lot between the ranger's station and the playground, near the swings. CLICK DIRECTLY ON THE MAP IF YOU THINK YOU ARE LOST. IT WILL BRING YOU RIGHT TO US WHERE WE MEET.
Start Time: We will start hiking promptly at the scheduled time.
Duration of the walk – depends on the people and dogs in the group. We frequently end up walking in smaller packs based on the comfort level of the participants.
In the past this walk takes about 1 hour, and longer for time spent in the open fields.
Please remember pooh bags and that your dog must be on a leash that is no more than 10 feet long.

item.title: Dillsburg Game Night - Calvary Methodist Church in the Family Center — Wed Aug 12, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Central PA Game Club Dillsburg Game Night meets every Wednesday from 6:30-9:30pm for casual tabletop games. We’ve been going strong since 2016, and most Wednesdays you’ll find about 30-40 gamers who love to learn and teach new games. It’s a great group of friendly people.
Given the timeframe, most of the games played are light to medium Euros, although many of us also love card games (including trick-taking games) and party games. We have a library of about 200 games available to play, and people typically bring their own games as well.
We also run long game days (typically every other month, usually a Saturday 2-9pm) and other special events. Join us on Facebook or Discord for more information about those.
Attendees do not often RSVP on Meetup. It may show 1 person is coming but we have 40 people every Wednesday and will cancel the event if it is not happening. Feel free to message with questions.
Cost: Free Who: All Ages (15 and under must be accompanied by an adult) When: Every

item.title: Third Story Artist Talk and Book Signing with Sarah Bourne Rafferty — Sat Aug 15, 10:30 AM — Third Story Art
item.description: Sarah Bourne Rafferty will be joining Third Story for a free Artist’s Talk, followed by a book-signing of her beautiful new book, “Botanical Cyanotype: A Guide to the Art of Sun Printing” Sarah has an MFA in Printmaking and Book Arts from The University of the Arts. In addition to creating the original cyanotypes that drive Atwater Designs, she is an educator and creative mentor. She has work in our current gallery exhibit, Tapestry, as well as unframed, original cyanotypes in our flat file. Sarah is one of Third Story Art’s favorite artists to talk with about creativity, studio practices, motivation and mind set. We know this talk is going to be great! And of course, we will also be talking about Sarah’s new book: “Botanical Cyanotype: a Guide to the Art of Sun Printing” Sarah will be signing books following our discussion. item.title: The Brave World of Peace-building for Israelis & Palestinians — Tue Aug 25, 7:00 PM — Congregation Shaarai Shomayim
item.description:
On August 25, Rabbi Paskoff will share reflections from his recent trip to Israel, his fifth visit since the war began on October 7, 2023. During his visits, he has spent time with grassroots organizations bringing Israelis and Palestinians together for peacebuilding, as well as Israeli human rights organizations. Join Rabbi Paskoff for a Q&A session about what he has learned through these experiences, with an opportunity to listen, ask questions, and learn more about the work being done toward peace and human rights. Advance registration is required for security purposes, and attendees are encouraged to submit questions in advance. We welcome our congregation and community to join this opportunity for thoughtful conversation and learning.
Source: Church of the Apostles UCC

item.title: Columbia Public Library Friends Group Meeting — Wed Aug 26, 6:00 PM — Columbia
item.description:
Community, Adults, Seniors
If you have a spare hour or two a week, we invite you to join the “Little Library that Could” as we expand our reach and services in 2026 during Columbia’s 300th Anniversary. We are launching a Friends Group to take some of the pressure off our dedicated staff. It’s a great way to make new friends, share your interests with others, and help the library expand its footprint in the communities we serve.If any of these planned projects grab your interest, consider joining them at their next meeting!Cataloging our collection Columbia History ArtifactsAssembling themed displays at the Market HouseSupercharge Adult Game NightWork on Outdoor Landscaping and BeautificationResearch and Write About Columbia HistoryBook Delivery to the Elderly and InfirmJump-Start Special Interest Book ClubsVolunteer for Special Community Outreach Projectsand more!
Source: Lancaster Libraries

item.title: Compline, Ancient Music for the Modern Soul — Fri Aug 7, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Compline, Ancient Music for the Modern Soul In-person and streamed Click here to view the streaming service. The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 9:00 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are sung or chanted as night falls by an ensemble of approximately 25 accomplished a capella singers drawn from around the Central Pennsylvania region.
Source: Saint James Lancaster
